audio_caption: The audio begins with a male speaker addressing an audience, stating he has something to tell them. His tone is conversational and slightly anticipatory. He describes playing on his computer and noticing something moving quickly out of the corner of his eye and uses a flashlight. He admits he can't really explain it. He says he's going to show the audience, and then there's a brief shuffling noise.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker inviting someone to "see something", emphasizing that "this is something, something to see". He sounds excited and possibly surprised. The speaker then directs attention to an object, stating "look at this thing", and remarks that "this thing is huge", further stating that he has "never seen this before".

The audio clip features a single male speaker expressing fear and disgust while observing something. He describes it as looking like it "wants to kill" him, noting "the spikes on his legs," emphasizing that "it's huge" and "it's alive." His tone is anxious and apprehensive. No music or other distinct sounds are present.

The audio clip begins with a single male speaker, his tone hushed as he observes something he advises not to move. He indicates he is filming a video, and then states "this is supposed to be the end of it". He proceeds to describe the front and back of an object, noting the back looks like the front to help with disguise from predators. His tone shifts, asserting that despite its appearance, he has done his research.

The clip begins with a male speaker identifying "number one," stating it's "a female" house centipede. He explains that they can be distinguished by "the very last two legs on it," and points out the front with "little eyes." He then describes the back of the centipede, noting "the top two legs, they extend out extremely long." The audio fades slightly toward the end of the clip.

The clip begins with a male speaker mentioning "funny things" and exclaiming "Oh shit" as a woman begins moving. The speaker refers to something he calls "a monster" but then says it is supposedly "harmless," although he believes it "doesn't look harmless." He then shifts focus to "my point." The male speaker expresses concern about something "jumping on me." It transitions to the male speaker saying, "Little talk ladies and gentlemen."

The clip starts with one male speaker. He relays some information, starting with, "I looked it up online and guess what it says". He says it is "harmless", and "extremely harmless", even saying it is "beneficial" to have in your house. He justifies this statement, saying "it eats ants, roaches, spiders, bees, anything". He finishes by saying "okay?".

The audio clip features a single male speaker with a conversational tone, initially advising listeners not to be alarmed if they see a centipede in their house, asserting that it provides pest control and is harmless, despite its scary appearance. The speaker acknowledges its unsettling looks at the end. No music is present, and background or ambient sounds are not discernible, nor are any other types of sound effects.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker stating "my actually" before correcting himself, indicating he thinks a specific insect is doing "push-ups" to get stronger. He continues to say that even if you wanted to kill it, you probably couldn't because it's so fast. He recalls seeing it zoom across his wall, which scared him.

The audio begins with a speaker stating "But they're harmless." The speaker continues, explaining that they eat spiders, ants, and roaches, implying that their presence indicates other pests. The speaker, who seems to be a male, then mentions having ants downstairs and that they eat spiders.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker expressing a thought, starting with "being at this thing up here" and then contemplating how it won't bite him, unlike a spider which can "tear your ass up". The tone is casual and slightly humorous, before changing to a practical note that he is taking it to the basement to eat spiders, adding a piece of "informing insight".

The audio clip starts with a male speaker advising the listener to not be alarmed if they see "one of these big things" because "it's extremely fast" and "it's not nothing to be harm, it can't harm you." He offers to prove his statement by looking it up. The speaker then seems to be typing into a search engine, specifically typing "house centipede." After a brief pause, the speaker makes an affirmative sound, "hmm, okay."

The clip begins with a male speaker, who sounds like he is speaking naturally, then starts to say "our house...", and adds "are house centipedes dangerous to humans?" as the topic. He continues with an "okay" and starts speaking again, mentioning a picture shown. The speaker then says, "It's the same as that thing," and after a brief pause, says "and let's see". He then says "okay" again, followed by a short "beep" sound.

The audio clip starts with one male speaker reading research information, mentioning a creature that is "predatory on other arthropods, including cockroaches, nymphs, flies, moth, bedbugs, crickets, silverfish, earwigs and small spiders," speaking in a clear and informative tone.

The clip begins with a male speaker discussing insects, including what people might not want in their homes. He reads from "Bug Guide", an approved site, stating it's useful for identifying unfamiliar insects. He notes that the site says that these insects are beneficial because they rid the home of other pests. The man mentions that centipedes are aggressive predators and that their jaws cannot easily pierce human skin. He acknowledges the statement makes him nervous, but he wants the centipede to stay so it can help rid the home of other pests. The man concludes by saying "just so you know, insight."

The clip begins with a male speaker, expressing mild anxiety about a bug, saying "Don't be scared", but then admitting "I'm scared a lot" before trying to joke about it. He ends with "Peace out". A brief shuffling or rustling sound occurs.
